findings.text: The live-census paragraph states '9 delivered runs owe an obligation, each with its reason', but the log it names (live-census-20261117T2145Z.log) carries 8 entries in its obligations array (grep -c '"age_seconds"' = 8, and the parsed JSON's len(obligations) = 8); 9 is counts.unrequested, one of which is younger than the 600 s deadline and so owes nothing yet. The example reasons are also not the log's: the eight entries give 'the run has no live pointer', 'the resumed attempt has not delivered', 'the run is a measurement run', 'the review reflex recorded skipped' and 'the review reflex recorded lane-paused', while the text names 'a review the resume superseded', which appears in no obligation. A reader checking the receipt the paragraph itself names finds a different count and different reasons, which is the same defect class the increment's gate and negative-control paragraphs were rewritten to clear.

No test asserts that a figure in this fragment equals a summary line in the log it names, which is why the gate paragraph could cite '68 passed in 47.3 s at f4a8ef887b' through a promotion gate and the census paragraph could keep 9 against a log of 8; the fragment's numbers are guarded by review reading alone.

The artifacts line repeats '9 obligations' beside the same 2145Z census whose obligations array holds 8, so the manifest carries the fragment's unreceipted figure as well and will repeat it into the landed record.
